title: The Fiscal Emergency
dialogue: Elara Vostane does not wait to be summoned. She is already in your office when you arrive, a single ledger open on your desk. She has underlined one number three times.
monologue: I know what number it is before I look.

vostane_numbers.speaker: elara_vostane
vostane_numbers.dialogue: The deficit has crossed the point where I can manage it quietly, Chancellor. Debt service alone will consume more than a quarter of next year's revenue if this continues. I have three options. None of them are good. All of them are better than pretending this isn't happening.

vostane_options.speaker: elara_vostane
vostane_options.dialogue: Emergency austerity — immediate cuts across every ministry, effective next week. It will work. It will also make you very unpopular very quickly. Continued borrowing — we manage the immediate crisis but the debt compounds, and eventually someone else asks the question I'm asking you now. Or — public acknowledgment. Tell the country the truth, ask for patience, and accept that patience is not something the opposition will grant you.

final_deficit_choice.speaker: narrator
final_deficit_choice.dialogue: Vostane waits. She has already decided which option she thinks is correct. She has not said which one.

choices.text: Order emergency austerity across every ministry.

reactions.text: It will hold the line. It will not make anyone love you for it.

journalEntry.title: The Fiscal Emergency
journalEntry.content: I ordered the cuts. Vostane says it was correct. The workers' coalition will not see it that way, and they will not be wrong to feel abandoned.

reactions.text: Then we are borrowing against a future Chancellor's patience, not just their treasury.

journalEntry.title: The Fiscal Emergency
journalEntry.content: I chose to borrow rather than cut. Vostane did not argue. She simply wrote the number down and underlined it again, for whoever reads this ledger next.

reactions.text: That is either the bravest thing you've done in this office, or the most reckless. I genuinely don't know which yet.

journalEntry.title: The Fiscal Emergency
journalEntry.content: I told them the truth. The Herald will not be kind about it tomorrow. Neither, I suspect, will history — one way or the other.
